response.title: which dehumidifiers can pump water up and out a basement window
response.answer:
You want a dehumidifier with a built-in condensate pump, which can automatically push collected water upward through a hose and out a basement window.

Unlike regular dehumidifiers that rely on gravity drainage, these can pump water vertically, so you don't need a floor drain or to empty a bucket.

For your setup, the most important specification is vertical pump lift (sometimes called pump height or pumping distance).

Look for:

Built-in pump: Automatically pumps water out when the collection reservoir reaches a certain level.

Vertical lift of 10–16 feet or more: Usually sufficient to reach a basement window.

Continuous pump drainage: Runs automatically without manually emptying the tank.

50-pint capacity: A good starting point for a moderately damp basement.

How the drainage works
Illustration: the pump pushes water up through a small hose and out the window.

For a permanent installation, route the hose through a sealed window insert, slope the exterior end away from the house, and discharge somewhere water won't flow back toward the foundation. In freezing weather, an outdoor hose can ice up and block drainage.

That will help determine whether a standard built-in pump is sufficient or whether you need a higher-lift option.
